attributes.description:
BYOT is a native client for OpenCode, the open-source coding agent. Connect to the OpenCode server running on your own computer and drive coding sessions from your iPhone or iPad.

Browse projects and sessions, send prompts with photos or files, and watch assistant text, reasoning, and tool activity stream live. Inspect tool inputs, progress, output, and errors. Answer permission requests and questions from your server, queue follow-up prompts, and choose models from your server's catalog. Review session diffs when your server supports them.

Switch between saved servers, group sessions by project or browse them in one list, and find sessions by title, project, or path. Unsent text and attachments stay on this iPhone across session changes and app relaunches. Choose System, Light, or Dark appearance.

With the optional BYOT companion running on your computer, get notifications for approvals, questions, completed turns, and errors. Enable the computer queue to keep accepted prompts running in order while BYOT is closed. Your computer must remain awake and the companion connected. Work that has not finished uploading needs BYOT to reconnect; uncertain delivery requires your review.

BYOT supports OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2 beta servers with automatic protocol detection. Available features depend on the server version; some OpenCode 2 beta servers do not expose per-session diffs.

Your server does the work. BYOT renders its responses and sends your instructions over HTTPS. There is no BYOT account or sign-up, and no tracking. Anonymous usage data is off until you turn it on, and it never includes your prompts, code, server addresses, or project names. Server passwords are stored in the iOS Keychain. In direct mode, prompts and attachments go to your configured server and the model providers you enable there. Optional notifications and the computer queue use the BYOT relay for device registration, delivery, and encrypted queued content. See the privacy policy for storage and retention details.

Requires an OpenCode server you operate, reachable over HTTPS, for example through Tailscale. Notifications and the computer queue also require the BYOT companion. BYOT is an independent client and is not affiliated with the OpenCode project.
attributes.promotionalText: Drive OpenCode from your iPhone or iPad: live sessions, ! shell mode, a real terminal, colored diff review, and one-tap approvals from notifications.
attributes.whatsNew:
Fixes for screens that reacted badly to being left mid-load:

- Leaving the projects screen while it was still loading could leave an error message and a blank workspace behind. A cancelled request is no longer treated as a failure, so the last known state stays put.
- Saved sessions now say "Connecting" while byot reaches your server, instead of "Status unavailable". A sleeping computer could leave every row reading "Status unavailable" for up to a minute. "Status unavailable" is now kept for a server that answered with an error, and that project shows the reason.
- While the "Showing sessions saved ..." notice is up, rows show no status, since none is known.
- The camera, microphone, speech recognition and local network prompts now always show their explanation in English as well as Simplified Chinese.
- If you have anonymous usage data on, leaving the session list mid-load no longer counts as a network error, and the server you connect to is counted correctly when you opt in during that launch.
